title: Huns
capsule: The Huns were a nomadic confederacy first attested in Chinese sources as a separate group from the Xiongnu, who migrated westward and appeared north of the Caspian Sea by the 370s CE; this dataset records them from 106 to 425. Under Attila (r. 434–453), who murdered his brother Bleda around 445 to rule alone, the Hunnic confederation reached its greatest extent, extracting tribute from the Eastern Roman Empire and devastating Gaul and northern Italy. After Attila's death in 453 his sons contested power; subject Germanic peoples revolted at the Battle of Nedao (454), and the western Hunnic empire dissolved within a generation. Eastern Hunnic groups persisted on the Pontic steppe until absorbed by successor confederacies.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Hunnic territorial extent is highly conjectural; the western empire's core in Pannonia is well-supported by Roman sources, but steppe frontiers from the Caspian to the Danube reflect scholarly inference from narrative sources rather than administrative records.
